chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mansur, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man asked him about the Turks who raid the Muslims and take their children, and then the Muslims capture them; are they returned to them? He said, 'Yes, and the Muslim is the brother of the Muslim, and the Muslim has more right to his property wherever he finds it.'

key_terms.التُّرْكِ: The Turks (a specific group of non-Muslims mentioned in the context of raiding)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Muslim children captured by non-Muslims?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the precedence of Muslim kinship over non-Muslim captors regarding the restitution of children and property. The Imam grounds this legal ruling in the broader theological principle of *ukhuwwah* (brotherhood), asserting that a Muslim’s claim to their own is superior regardless of location or circumstance. This serves as a foundational precedent in Shia jurisprudence for resolving disputes of custody and ownership in times of conflict.
